Standard: Vehicle control function driven requirements and interfaces are established and flowed to the integrated subsystems (e.g., electrical power, hydraulics, avionics, propulsion, ECS). These requirements capture worst-case operational scenarios, for both nominal (un-failed) and failure conditions, to ensure VCF performance is maintained. Vehicle control function functional performance is demonstrated in all worst-case nominal and degraded conditions. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Vehicle control function requirements and interface documents with all integrated subsystems capture VCF driving requirements and interfaces and are configuration controlled. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis to support VCF driving requirements and interfaces for integrated subsystems is performed. Analysis shows that margins are maintained during worst-case operational scenarios (e.g., hydraulic demand, electrical power, cooling) including, but not limited to the following considerations: a. Hydraulic capacity is assessed in worst-case nominal (un-failed) and hydraulic degraded conditions and requirements and interfaces coordinated with the hydraulics domain. Hydraulic source switching transients are analyzed to assess hydraulic switching timing. b. Uninterruptible electrical power is assessed to maintain all VCF critical systems in all worst-case nominal and electrical power degraded conditions, including air vehicle start-up, and requirements and interfaces coordinated with the electrical power domain. Vehicle control function electrical loads required on emergency power are analyzed to ensure electrical capacity is available to support emergency scenarios. c. Cooling is assessed to enable continuous VCF component operation under worst-case nominal conditions. Upon total loss of cooling, critical VCF components operate without degradation for the period of time it takes to land the air vehicle under worst-case operating conditions. Test.
    (1) Ground or Lab test: Hardware-in-the-loop test (e.g., HITL labs, Iron Bird, air vehicle ground test) verifies VCF functionality and interfaces with all integrated subsystems for nominal (un-failed), worst-case performance.
    (2) Lab test: Failure modes and effects testing verifies VCF functional performance in failed and degraded conditions to include backup configurations and in emergency conditions.
    (3) Lab test: Following total loss of cooling, thermal testing demonstrates critical VCF components operate without degradation for the period of time it takes to land the air vehicle under worst-case operating conditions.
